title: IPL 2026 Final and Season Awards
text:
Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) retained the Indian Premier League (IPL) title after beating Gujarat Titans (GT) by five wickets in the IPL 2026 final at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad. It was RCB's second straight final, and they became only the third franchise to win back-to-back titles, after Chennai Super Kings and Mumbai Indians. They had won their first trophy in 2025.

The season had opened on 28 March at the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru, where RCB hosted Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH).

Batting first in the final, GT scored 155 for eight in their 20 overs. RCB reached 161 for five in reply, with 12 balls to spare.

The two finalists had already met in Qualifier 1 at Dharamshala on Tuesday, 26 May. RCB made 254 for five and won by 92 runs. Rajat Patidar, the RCB captain, was unbeaten on 93 off 33 balls.

Four teams reached the playoffs from the league stage. RCB, GT and SRH each finished on 18 points, with RCB top on net run rate. Rajasthan Royals (RR) took the last spot with 16 points. RR had sealed their place on 24 May with a 30-run win over Mumbai Indians (MI) at the Wankhede Stadium, their final league match. RR scored 205 for eight after recovering from 119 for five, and MI were held to 175 for nine. Punjab Kings and Kolkata Knight Riders were eliminated.

In the Eliminator on 27 May, RR beat SRH by 47 runs. Rajasthan made 243 for eight in 20 overs, with Rajasthan opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scoring 97 off 29 balls, including 12 sixes. SRH were bowled out for 196 in 19.2 overs, and their season ended there.

Qualifier 2 was played at Mullanpur on Friday, 29 May. Rajasthan made 214 for six, and GT reached 219 for three in 18.4 overs to win by seven wickets. Shubman Gill scored 104 off 53 balls, and the win sent GT into the final against RCB.

Sooryavanshi, aged 15, won the Orange Cap with 776 runs in 16 matches, becoming the youngest winner of the award. Gill finished second on the run charts, and Sai Sudharsan of Gujarat Titans third. Sooryavanshi also broke Chris Gayle's record for the most sixes in a season, surpassing the 59 Gayle hit in 2012. He was named the Most Valuable Player and the Emerging Player of the Season, and also won the Super Striker and Super Sixes awards.

Sai Sudharsan hit the most fours of the season, while Mohammed Siraj bowled the most dot balls of any bowler. Manish Pandey of Kolkata Knight Riders won the Catch of the Season award.

questions.q: Which franchise did Kagiso Rabada play for when he won the IPL Purple Cap in 2020?
questions.explanation: Rabada took 30 wickets for Delhi Capitals in IPL 2020 and won the Purple Cap for that season.

questions.q: Who won the IPL Purple Cap for the 2021 season?
questions.explanation: Harshal Patel, playing for Royal Challengers Bangalore, took 32 wickets in IPL 2021 to win the Purple Cap.

Tanvir won the 2008 Purple Cap for Rajasthan Royals, RP Singh the 2009 cap for Deccan Chargers, Bhuvneshwar Kumar the 2017 cap for Sunrisers Hyderabad and Imran Tahir the 2019 cap for Chennai Super Kings.

questions.assertion: Virat Kohli was named Player of the Match in the IPL 2026 final.
questions.reason: Mohammed Shami won the IPL Purple Cap in 2024.
questions.explanation: The assertion is true: Kohli was named Player of the Match after an unbeaten 75 off 42 balls. The reason is false: Shami won the Purple Cap in 2023 with Gujarat Titans, and a different bowler won it in 2024.

statements: I. Dwayne Bravo won the IPL Purple Cap in 2016.
II. Kagiso Rabada won the IPL Purple Cap in 2025.
questions.explanation: Neither is correct. The 2016 Purple Cap went to Bhuvneshwar Kumar, and the 2025 cap went to Prasidh Krishna.

statements: I. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi comes from Bihar.
II. Lasith Malinga won the IPL Purple Cap in 2011 while playing for Mumbai Indians.
III. Morne Morkel won the IPL Purple Cap in 2012 while playing for Chennai Super Kings.
questions.explanation: Sooryavanshi is from Tajpur in Samastipur district, Bihar, and Malinga won the 2011 cap for Mumbai Indians. Morkel won the 2012 cap for Delhi Daredevils, not Chennai Super Kings.
